Requesting Sub-Accounts from NinjaTrader

Only follow this guide if your funded account is over $60,000. If you have $60,000 or less in your live account, you do not need sub-accounts and should skip this guide.

This walks you through requesting additional sub-accounts once your main NinjaTrader account is funded. Sub-accounts let you diversify across more of the algo suite, but NinjaTrader reviews every request individually and can be strict about approving them.

If you wish to see the walkthrough video, you can watch it here. Otherwise, the steps below have you covered. Your progress is saved on this device.

0 of 5 steps complete

Tick each step as you go.

  1. 1

    Confirm you actually need a sub-account

    0:00 to 1:20

    NinjaTrader has strict, largely unwritten policies about approving sub-account requests, so you should only ask for one if you have the capital to justify it. If you only have around $50,000 to $60,000 total, you do not need to open sub-accounts. The value of sub-accounts comes from spreading your capital across more of the algo suite for stronger diversification.

    1. Use the cash account tool at ninjatradertrading.com/cash-accounts to see how your current capital maps to the available algorithms.
    2. If splitting your capital across a main account and one or more sub-accounts gets you closer to full algo coverage, a sub-account is worth requesting.
    3. If you are under roughly $60,000 total, skip this and just run everything from your main account.
  2. 2

    Make sure the money is already in your live account

    1:20 to 2:40

    You cannot request a sub-account until your live account (not the demo/SIM account) actually holds the cash you intend to move. Your total capital gets split evenly across your main account and every sub-account you open, so decide up front how many accounts you are running and divide from there.

    1. Complete the funding steps from the Fund Your Account guide first, using your live account.
    2. Confirm your live account balance shows a dollar amount greater than zero before requesting a sub-account.
    3. Plan the split before you request anything. Capital is divided equally across the main account and each sub-account, never lopsided.
    4. Examples: $60,000 becomes $30,000 in the main account and $30,000 in one sub. $90,000 becomes $30,000 each across the main and two subs. $200,000 becomes $50,000 each across the main and three subs.
    5. Three sub-accounts is the ceiling, so four accounts total. Above that, the per-account allocation simply grows.

    IRA and Roth accounts work differently. For retirement accounts, every allocation has to land on a multiple of $15,000. Round your even split to the nearest $15,000 increment before you submit, since an amount that does not fall on that multiple will not go through.

  3. 3

    Prepare your reason, referencing CFTC Regulation 1.46

    2:40 to 5:10

    NinjaTrader is cautious about CFTC Regulation 1.46, which restricts using multiple accounts to hold offsetting long and short positions. Every request is reviewed individually by a person, not an automated check, so wording matters and outcomes can vary between reviewers even for similar requests.

    1. Use one of the reason templates below as your starting point.
    2. Reword it in your own words (running it through a tool like ChatGPT to rephrase while keeping the same structure and reasoning works well) so it does not look copy-pasted.
    3. Keep the core point intact: this account will not be used to maintain offsetting long and short positions, in line with CFTC Regulation 1.46.

    Vincere reason templates. Use the one that matches what you are opening, then lightly reword it.

    Sub-account 1

    Diversification across algorithm suite

    I am requesting this additional account to trade a distinct subset of our algorithm suite that requires separate capital allocation for proper risk management. This account will not be used to maintain offsetting long and short positions, consistent with the restrictions of CFTC Regulation 1.46.

    Sub-account 2

    Separate instrument focus

    This account is being opened to focus capital on a different set of instruments than my existing account, allowing each account to run its own independent strategy. I confirm this account will not be used to maintain offsetting long and short positions, per CFTC Regulation 1.46.

    Sub-account 3

    Independent risk allocation

    I am opening this account to isolate risk and margin usage for a separate strategy allocation, keeping it independent from my other trading accounts. This account will not be used to hold offsetting long and short positions, in accordance with CFTC Regulation 1.46.

    Caution: do not submit these templates word for word. Reviewers see the same copy-pasted paragraphs constantly, and identical wording is a fast route to a denial. Run your chosen template through ChatGPT or Claude with a prompt like "reword this in my own voice, keep the meaning and the CFTC Regulation 1.46 reference intact," or simply rewrite it yourself. Keep the substance, change the words.

  4. 4

    Submit the request from Settings

    5:10 to 6:45

    The request form lives in the same Accounts settings page you used to fund your account. Filling it out correctly the first time, with Speculation as the margin type, gives you the best shot at approval.

    1. Go to your NinjaTrader account, click your profile icon in the top right, then Settings.
    2. On the Accounts tab, click the blue Add Trading Account button.
    3. In the Name field, type your own name exactly as it appears on your NinjaTrader account. The field often looks like your name is already filled in, but that text is only a placeholder. You have to actually type it in yourself or the form will not accept the request.
    4. Set Margin Type to Speculation (not Hedge).
    5. Paste your reworded reason into the Reason field.
    6. Enter the transfer amount as your equal share, meaning your total capital divided by the number of accounts you are running, main account included.
    7. Leave 'Will there be an authorized party other than the account owner' set to No, unless that genuinely applies to you.
    8. Open every agreement and disclosure document attached to the request and read through them. Several will not register as acknowledged until you actually open them, and an unopened document will hold up or void your submission.
    9. Click Add Account to submit.

    Caution: the Name field only looks pre-filled. What you see there is placeholder text, not a real entry. Type your name in manually, matching your NinjaTrader account exactly, no nickname, shortened version, or made-up account label. Assuming it is already filled in is one of the most common reasons these requests get bounced back.

  5. 5

    Know the limits and what to do if you are denied

    6:45 to end

    You can have a total of three sub-accounts plus your main account, for four accounts total. Denials are common and not personal, since two people can submit nearly identical reasons and get different reviewers with different judgment calls.

    1. You can hold a maximum of one main account plus three sub-accounts (four total).
    2. Open one sub-account at a time: request one, wait two to three business days for approval, then request the next if you need it.
    3. If a request is denied, take the same reasoning, have it reworded again, and resubmit. It is normal to need several tries before approval.
    NinjaTrader will not tell you the specific reason for a denial. Resubmitting with reworded but substantively identical reasoning is expected practice, not a workaround.

  6. Sub-account request submitted

    Once approved, use the cash account Algo Distribution Calculator to plan how capital and algorithms split across your main account and new sub-account.
